notes.title: Patch 6 - The Big One!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40377373/faad5de2e1659baff56e6db8c97980d77b5e2c2b.png[/img]

Fellow Survivors,

We’re excited to reveal our latest content update for Serum, this adds more of the road map content we revealed during the early access launch. Patch 6 is quite possibly our biggest update so far, and brings a lot of new player focused enhancements, and brought about some fixes that should iron out those performance issues some players were encountering. Tackling optimisation fixes was a much larger task than we first anticipated since it meant really getting under the hood of he game.

In addition to the new content, and performance tweaks, we’ve also been able to implement lots of other fixes to the game as well, and these addressed areas such as item storage, Inventory, missing localized text, UI and visual elements which should also make a big difference.

In patch 6 we’ve added Steam achievements and there are 23 to obtain in Serum. These achievements include various tasks such as finding the Pilot, defeating the formidable Alpha Wolf, recycling 100 items to gain valuable components, collecting all available files in the archive, and utilizing the Absorber 30 times among many others to obtain.

Based on player feedback you’ll be pleased to know that the Player difficulty level can now be customised giving you the option to adjust the level of challenge you’d prefer.
Included in this latest content patch are Combat traps providing you with even more tactical options against the creatures that roam Serums dangerous world.

Lastly, we’ve also added additional language support in addition to the 9 languages the game currently supports,

Let us know what you think of the update in our [url=https://discord.gg/fvuWbPMb66]Discord channel[/url].

Also, be sure to check out our latest Serum game stream on Serum’s official steam page where we go over all the recent updates including the new freestanding absorbers, trap placement function, achievements and the new combat traps.

notes.title: Survive or Die Fighting: Revealing the Lethal Realities of Combat
notes.content:
In the devastated world of Serum, mutated monstrosities lurk in the darkness, and death is only one false step away. Mutated beasts and even plants that have been infected by the Blight will hunger for your flesh to kill or injure you. Arm yourself with our combat essential guide to keep you safe.
 
Prepare yourselves for the inevitable combat that lays ahead as we reveal the combat essentials to your survival:
 
[h3]COMBAT ESSENTIALS GUIDE[/h3]
 
The test of a true survivor is their ability to handle threats, in Serum you’re going to come up against many different kinds, all hell bent on your untimely demise. Here’s some combat essentials to keep you safe.
 
[b]Choose wisely[/b] – Use the right type of weapon against certain adversaries, the bow is great at creating distance between you and danger, but a machete blade deals a hefty blow up close.
 
[b]Upgrade[/b] – Utilise serum and components to upgrade your weapons as soon as you can, things like serum enhanced arrows can make a real difference in combat.
 
[b]Timing [/b]– Tentarats spit a toxic substance, so time your attacks carefully before they can muster up another dose to fire at you.
 
[b]Combine weapons[/b] – Use your bow to initiate a first blood strike at distance before using melee weapons to finish the kill up close.
 
[b]Spear it [/b]– The spear has been trusted for centuries, it will also serve you well in Serum as a mid-range weapon to use, especially against Fog wolves.
 
[b]Use Cover[/b] – Cars, barricades and trees can provide essential cover from line-of-sight attackers, use cover to avoid confrontation or as a protective barrier from danger.
 
[b]Beware of pack animals [/b]– Pick your fights carefully, some mutated creatures attack in packs, getting overwhelmed you’re as good as dead.
 
[b]Tread lightly [/b]– Craft Serum blends to enhance abilities that can provide essential boosts, a silent stalking ability to reduce noise for example can be a lifesaver.
 
[b]Night vision [/b]– Create a serum brew that lets you see in the dark, get the advantage in low light situations.
 
[b]Block and Dodge[/b] – Utilise your melee weapons to block and dodge lethal attacks to stay in the fight longer. Look for patterns in the attack to defend against and time your blocks.

notes.title: Serum Early Access Roadmap
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40377373/006664a23ca74b86f3879db240e5f40269c35bbb.png[/img]

[h3]Fellow Survivors,[/h3]

Today, we wanted to share the content and features still to come for [b]Serum[/b] since we know that timely updates, fixes, and implementing community feedback are important to you, the player.

By far, the biggest decision has been to give co-op more time in development and integrate this later than planned within the early access window. While this may be disappointing to many of you, we feel it’s very important we can deliver updates and game content that live up to players' expectations because sacrificing the quality of the game is something we very much want to avoid.

The Serum roadmap below highlights the continued work going into Serum in the weeks and months ahead, leading up to the Version 1.0 release.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40377373/d28f10a112e2560371656faf496a6e1ec66adcd1.png[/img]

[b]Quality of Life Fixes[/b]

First and foremost, our focus is to implement a range of quality-of-life improvements for players as one of our first tasks on Serum. This includes [b]bug fixes[/b] and [b]additional languages[/b] and translations, and we’ll continually look at player feedback to implement these so that the player experience in Serum is optimised.

As our early access journey gets underway next on our list will be [b]achievements[/b] as we know that rewarding player interactions and milestones is important. We’ll also be looking to implement a [b]UI revamp[/b] to ensure that it’s consistently intuitive for players as they brew, craft and upgrade in the game.

Further down the road, the roadmap also plans on introducing new combat options with [b]combat traps[/b] allowing players to expand their arsenal of weapons with passive capability to trap adversaries in the game world.

[b]New Biome[/b]

Canyon will be the third biome for players to explore in addition to ground zero (the node), the forest area and the swamp maps that are currently available. Canyon will introduce some new challenging adversaries and a new level boss creature to defeat as part of the game's narrative. This is a dry, arid location that will challenge the player with additional side quests to seek out survivors and reveal much more about the mutagen storyline.

[b]Co-op mode[/b]

Co-op mode for up to 4 players gives survivors an opportunity to tackle Serum’s infected denizens as a team with friends. Player resources will be shared, and by working together, players can create their own strategies to maximize their effectiveness in the Serum world.

Of course, early access will see our ongoing work to balance the game, add new features, tweak existing ones, and optimize the overall game. Community feedback is still important, so do talk to us via Discord. We are listening.

In the depths of the wilderness, harvesting plants and extracting the organs of living creatures isn't just a means of sustenance—it's a pathway to unlocking the mysteries of [b]Serum[/b] brewing. Dubbed [b]"Mr. Hyde"[/b] by one of the [b]E.V.A.S.[/b] junior lab assistants, this abomination epitomizes the harrowing transformations wrought by Serum. While not all gorilla test subjects share its immense size, they exhibited a strength that defied comprehension, posing a formidable threat if underestimated.

[h3]Fellow Survivors,[/h3]

We are pleased to reveal the answers for our second questions and answers session for [b]Serum[/b]. We received many great questions from the community, and here is our pick of the best ones. Also, don’t forget to register for a chance to access the forthcoming [b]Serum Playtest[/b] here on Steam.

[b]Compared to the Next Fest demo the current Serum brewing UI looks different, has that changed?[/b]

We looked at the player feedback from the Steam Next Fest demo, and it was evident that we needed to improve how intuitive the crafting and brewing system was to use. We also wanted to make it easier to understand, so we’ve improved that aspect with a new format and layout, which players can explore in the forthcoming playtest.

[b]Where is the story of Serum set in terms of its location?[/b]

The story is set on a remote island known for its potent source of life-saving liquid, which is the key ingredient for serum. It's also where the EVAS Corporation set up its main base of operations and started its research to enhance the cure of Blight.

[b]How important are resources, is player progression tied directly to the brewing and crafting of Serum, do I need to craft and brew Serum?[/b]

The story hints at how important it is to utilize different resources found in the game world to survive, and we want players to explore and seek out those resources as they play. This includes organic material found in things like plants and animals that, when combined with other things found discarded in the world like batteries, nails, scrap metal, welding Electrodes etc, they all play a part in enhancing and upgrading your abilities and equipment, including upgrades to your base facilities. The serum brewing mechanic plays a big part in your survival and progression.

[b]How many different abilities based around Serum brewing will be possible?[/b]

The game's development extends beyond the initial Early Access release, so there’s no definite number of abilities at this point. We can only say that we already have a decent number ready, and all of them will be useful in both combat and exploration. We are always open to more suggestions from our players, and we will definitely consider adding more abilities based on player feedback.

[b]Why does the player character need to inject Serum to survive in the wilderness if animals don't rely on it to survive?[/b]

Like any other person in the game world, the character needs to inject Serum to counter the effects of The Blight. The animals and other enemies in Serum mutated due to the experimentation on Serum variants conducted by EVAS Corporation; hence, the substance has already altered their DNA, and they no longer require it. They have become a completely new species adapted to survive in the harsh post-apocalyptic environment.

[b]I noticed cable cars in the demo, can players transit between biomes using them?[/b]

We’re not going to spoil that for players, but let’s just say it's well worth investigating when you play the game.

[b]How would you position Serum, is it biopunk or sci-fi?[/b]

Serumis definitely inspired by science fiction in relation to its themes. The story is set in the future but has aspects that still keep it quite relevant and grounded, so it still has that appeal and familiarity. Serum could be classed as a kind of Biopunk story, given that the story hints at the implications of biotechnology, not to mention the mutated creatures you’ll encounter.

[b]Are there any plans for a beta version?[/b]

We have just announced a playtest starting on April 24th which will last for a whole week. We're keen for players to test and help us with constructive feedback and insights for early access. If you missed the chance to play the Steam Next Fest demo, then the Serum playtest is a great opportunity to try the game and tell us what you think.

Want to be a part of the forthcoming [b]Serum Playtest?[/b] register on our Steam page for a chance to join in and help shape the game for early access.

notes.title: We're answering your questions!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40377373/3691a2461c5d949caca40e55ab5a9ab9915fceb9.png[/img]

Thank you for your interest and questions about [b]Serum[/b]. We were inundated with so many to be able to answer them all, but here are answers to some of the more popular ones.

[b]How will melee combat function? [/b]
The combat in Serum is based around melee and range attacks. The players will be able to craft multiple weapons and choose the best one to face various enemies who are susceptible to different types of damage. Each melee weapon will have a basic attack and a strong attack. As the players progress through the game, they will be able to upgrade the previously crafted weapons and repair them.

[b]Will there be the option to target lock and block?[/b]
There will be an option to block the attacks, but to ensure a free flow of combat, there will be no target lock.

[b]Will there be a story-driven DLC that emphasizes hardcore gameplay within the sci-fi (horror) world?[/b]
Serum is a story-driven game from the start. There may be further expansions that will enhance the experience by adding additional content, but it’s still too early to say.

[b]Is there a mode that's not cooperative-based, without an excessive focus on crafting, base-building, and extensive customization?[/b]
As a story-driven survival game, the game is focused on crafting and brewing mechanics that are tied to the player’s progress throughout the story. Various assets and adversaries in the game are designed to encourage the players to be resourceful and explore the game word.

[b]Is it possible to sign up for the closed beta/alpha tests?[/b]
Not at the moment, but if the opportunity arises, we will make sure to let our community know about it. Please join our Discord and check for regular updates on our Steam page for further development news.

[b]In which engine is Serum produced?[/b]
Serum was initially developed in Unreal Engine 4, but we’ve decided that the best course of action will be to transpose the game to the latest version of the engine. Now, the game can be enjoyed using the latest technologies delivered by the power of Unreal Engine 5.

[b]What is the backstory of Serum?[/b]
The events in Serum take place in the near future, where the world as we know has been struck by a catastrophic event called The Blight. Due to the sickness caused by the event, the world’s population dwindled close to extinction. The only cure for the effects of The Blight is the mysterious Serum that the EVAS corporation used to develop the remedy.

[b]What is the Serum’s function in the game world?[/b]
Serum is the only cure for the effects of The Blight known to mankind. Depending on the type of sickness, people may require more potent variants of the remedy. After some time, it was discovered that extensive use of the Serum can cause suspicious mutations in living beings. Our story begins after a failed experiment to stop the effects of the mutation.

[b]When and where is the game set?[/b]
The game is set on an island where the main ingredient of the cure was initially discovered and where the EVAS corporation placed its base of operations in the year 2060.

[b]Will it come to consoles?
[/b]At this moment, our focus is on the Early Access version for PCs. We do, however, wish the game to be released on more platforms in the future.

[b]Will there be multiple difficulty settings?[/b]
The game will have only one difficulty setting that is tailored to suit more advanced and beginning players who are familiar with the survival genre.

[b]Is Serum compatible with Steam Deck?[/b]
At this moment, the game is not optimised to work with Steam Deck, but this may change before the planned release of the game in Early Access.

[b]How many different formulas of Serum can be created for players to utilize and benefit from?[/b]
We don’t want to spoil too much, but the ingredients for Serum can be gathered from many sources, and there will be a variety of formulas that the players can experiment with. Each one of those will come with its own set of benefits.

[b]How will co-op work in Serum, do players work together, and is there a different goal to the main story if playing in co-op?[/b]
The host of the co-op game will be playing as the main character of the story and have the same goals as if this were a single-player mode. The other players that join him will take on the roles of other survivors who join the player on his journey and work together to finish his task.

[b]Is there a Serum that extends the amount of time until you need to take your next dose?[/b]
The Serum brewed from the formulas discovered by the players can have various effects and extend the time needed before the next dose by a different amount of time.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40377373/c046544c201306501fef26f848b7aa7d768587f3.png[/img]

We wish you all [b]Happy Holidays[/b] and  [b]Happy New Year[/b] from all the teams at [b]Game Island[/b] and [b]Toplitz Productions[/b].

A sense of dread enveloped me as I entered the unfamiliar biome that can only be described as The Swamp. My search for more of the substance that had reshaped the world had led me here. I had to find more Serum. My heart raced, and my grip tightened around the handle of my makeshift axe as I took my first steps into the unknown.

As I waded through knee-deep water, I could smell the scent of decay coming from almost every direction. The leafless trees loomed overhead, their branches casting eerie shadows. I couldn't shake the feeling that every rustle in the underbrush and every ominous croak belonged to creatures altered by Serum.

A nervous chuckle escaped my lips as I mumbled to myself, "Hope there are no mutated mosquitoes here." The thought of facing grotesque, mutated bugs brought a smile to my face, a feeble attempt to mask the anxiety.

Suddenly, a low growl echoed through the swamp, freezing me in my tracks. I peered into the murky depths, my hand instinctively tightening around my axe. The water rippled, and from its depths emerged a massive creature. The Swamp had just unveiled its first secret.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40377373/7d953031f95dcf1c81c04bb3e9bb7383653885ec.png[/img]

[i]Near the ruins of an abandoned gas station, I caught sight of the Tentarats, a swift and deadly pack with toxic tricks up their sleeves. This place promised a potential solution, but the odds were stacked against me. Broken and battered, the gas station held the remnants of life before the catastrophe, now claimed by these agile creatures.

Their incredible speed and coordinated attacks posed a challenge. To make matters worse, their toxic spit could turn the battlefield into a lethal zone. Drawing near risked entanglement with their snout tentacles, a surefire path to serious harm. The air, already thick with tension, could become even deadlier if the Tentarats launched a barrage of their long-range attacks.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40377373/5b2a528c941aa1726be66699f494c91db025099d.gif[/img]

[i]As I stood there, contemplating a strategy to outsmart these formidable foes, the gas station offered a glimmer of hope. A scavenger's paradise, it held the promise of tools, weapons, and resources that could turn the tide. But like the dormant cable cars, resurrecting a plan wasn't as simple as it seemed.

I may not be a seasoned tactician, but survival has taught me to rely on instinct and ingenuity. With each encounter, a careful dance unfolded – a dance with danger. As I faced the Tentarats and the ruins of the gas station, I knew that overcoming this challenge would demand more than just brute force. If there's an escape from this perilous dance, I'll find it – my will and hope lighting the way through the shadows of the gas station ruins.[/i]

Its broken cables dangled lifelessly, contrasting the island's vibrant beauty. The notion of this once-thriving transportation network now being completely useless intrigued me. It could have been the ideal means to traverse the island, weaving through the treacherous swamps, dense forests, and gaping canyons that separated its diverse regions.

I couldn't help but wonder about the island's past right before the catastrophe, when the cable cars were filled with EVAS scientists, providing easy access to its various research stations. It would be great to have these working again, but this would be no easy task. Since I am no engineer, I must rely on my survival skills and instincts, carefully planning each excursion.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40377373/500dd3454429bb8e9f9a3389d3cada184381455b.png[/img]

[i]As I ventured through the desolate landscape, searching for more answers, I noticed a peculiar building. It looked similar to other facilities I have seen before, but this one had a big sign on the side that said “Human”. Within its ominous confines, I encountered a chilling sight—the lifeless bodies of fellow humans. Little did I know that this encounter would thrust me into a confrontation with an unfathomable danger, a new breed of terror that would test not only my physical abilities but also the depths of my moral fortitude.

No longer than a few seconds after the discovery, one of the corpses started moving and getting up. As I stood there completely paralyzed by shock, the reanimated human remains charged at me with haste. At that moment, my instincts kicked into overdrive, and I swiftly reacted to the impending threat. I struck out at the corpse, fighting to protect myself. The clash was brief yet gruelling, with adrenaline coursing through my veins. The encounter left me exhausted, physically and emotionally drained.

As I was trying to catch my breath, a heavy wave of guilt washed over me. These were not mutated creatures like the ones I had battled before. These were remnants of humanity, reanimated into a grotesque semblance of life. In my heart, I knew that ending their existence was a moral burden far weightier than any fight I had faced thus far.

Unable to find suitable words to describe these walking corpses, I settled on the term "zombies." It seemed fitting, capturing the surreal horror of the situation. In my mind, I began to speculate on their origin. Could they be the result of failed human trials conducted within this facility, a twisted experiment gone awry? The thought sent shivers down my spine, contemplating the depths of human desperation and the consequences of tampering with nature's delicate balance.[/i]

notes.title: Eve's Temptation
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40377373/a78b36263c2e037d68c30e3d39b67e71ca6b6c6f.png[/img]

[i]While exploring a decrepit laboratory, I stumbled upon a mysterious room filled with newspaper clips meticulously pinned to a corkboard. The tale, woven together with pieces of red string, revolved around the [b]EVAS[/b] corporation. Are they the ones responsible for what is happening to me? As I unravelled clues and bits of information, I saw a narrative that seemed straight out of a dystopian novel.

It all began in the middle of the 21st century when a sudden surge in pollution plagued the world. This catastrophic event triggered a toxic epidemic called [b]The Blight[/b]. [b]The Blight[/b] spread like wildfire, ravaging the planet with its deadly and unfamiliar diseases. It began its sinister conquest by targeting plants and animals, but it wasn't long before it started to affect humans, putting our kind on the brink of extinction.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40377373/fdd4aa81e76d0a98232e4b82d0635e16ad29cdbc.png[/img]

During this chaos, pharmaceutical corporations raced to discover a cure. My attention got turned to a firm known as [b]EVAS[/b]. This name instantly felt familiar as their logo was plastered on almost every document I have found so far. It turns out that the native inhabitants of this island showcased an astonishing immunity to the blight, and a team of [b]EVAS[/b] scientists was dispatched here to investigate.

The next part seems like something completely out of this world. I discovered that a powerful earthquake struck this region in the early 21st century, reshaping the landscape and giving birth to an extraordinary phenomenon. From the river coursing through the island emerged a mysterious substance – a greenish elixir possessing remarkable properties. 

The news of this anomaly spread, turning the island into a tourist hotspot for several years. The townsfolk even rebranded their sole settlement as the marketing-savvy [b]Green River[/b]. The water from this fabled river mirrored the miraculous effects of renowned mountain springs, strengthening the human body but falling short of miraculous healings. Eventually, the allure of [b]Green River[/b] diminished, and the medicinal wonders of this substance were forgotten. Only a few island inhabitants, along with the flora and fauna, continued to bask in its blessings.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40377373/8ab4e2fc471213cddb5872c481d5438742d32272.png[/img]

As the scientists of [b]EVAS[/b] delved into their research, they discovered that the greenish water held a miraculous substance – a panacea capable of not only curing the blight but also shielding against the epidemic. Fuelled by this groundbreaking revelation, [b]EVAS[/b] decided to start mass production. The substance was extracted from the river's waters, purified, and introduced to the market under the name [b]Serum[/b] – a beacon of hope, marking the arrival of a new generation of medicine.

From that moment on, [b]EVAS[/b] has become famous worldwide and started to introduce even more potent types of [b]Serum[/b]. Some could even alter the body functions – increase intelligence, speed, or in some cases – prolong life. Was I one of their guinea pigs? If only I could remember more about how and when I got here – and what has happened to this place. Let’s hope I’ll find more clues further on the way.[/i]

notes.title: Fight to the death
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40377373/a6e849f98369d498675a29ebc9cba3b919358c42.png[/img]

[i]On one of my latest excursions, I stumbled across a boar in a grotesque form that sent shivers down my spine. Its flesh was torn, exposing raw muscle, while its eyes glowed a haunting green. I knew that if I didn't fight, this beast would surely overpower me. 

As the creature charged towards me, I dodged its swipes, narrowly avoiding its razor-sharp tusks. Its strength was immense, and each blow felt like a sledgehammer against my body. I needed an advantage, something to level the playing field.

With a quick decision, I reached into my pack and retrieved a vial containing a mixture of [b]Serum[/b]. I injected it into my arm, feeling an immediate surge of power. My senses sharpened, my muscles tightened, and a newfound confidence coursed through my veins. I leaped towards the boar, my movements faster and more precise than ever before.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40377373/e5296bc143267decff9bcaf9084c96bbd204a648.png[/img]

With a series of calculated strikes, I managed to land blows on the boar, exploiting its weaknesses. The [b]Serum[/b] coursing through me heightened my reflexes, allowing me to dodge its attacks with ease. The fight raged on, and I could feel the strain on my body, but I refused to give up.

Summoning every ounce of strength, I launched a final, devastating attack. With a precise strike, I plunged my spear into the boar's exposed flank, piercing through its decaying flesh. The creature let out a loud shriek, and its body convulsed before collapsing to the ground.

I stood there, breathing heavily, my body covered in sweat and dirt. The fight had taken its toll on me, but I had emerged victorious. The Serum mixture had given me the edge I needed to defeat the mutated boar, but what will be the cost?

As I took a moment to recover, I kept thinking about other horrors this island could hold. Would I be able to survive the next encounter? Only time would tell. But for now, my victory over this beast was a testament to my will to survive in this unforgiving world of Serum-infested nightmares.[/i]

notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40377373/1123c8eadad086aaef132d393d357143c0f3ef34.png[/img]

[i]It wasn't long after I found myself stranded in this strange place before I stumbled upon the plans for a [b]Growing Table[/b]. Building this device would allow me access to a sustainable source of [b]Serum[/b] from plants already growing on this island. I had to make it my top priority to craft one.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40377373/94a27bebbf8c2ebd45d3998a92ec4e583f01298e.png[/img]

In my short time here, I’ve learned that [b]Serum[/b] running through the plants was essential for survival on the island. The flora doesn’t offer much in quantity of the substance, but with enough plants, I can get ready for excursions deeper into the unknown.

Growing the plants turned out to be an easy task, but In the long run, I needed a more reliable source. The [b]Growing Table[/b] lamps consume a lot of power, and that is a scarce resource in this forsaken place. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40377373/e78276591c3e6fbc506366d720fda7db8ac8606c.png[/img]

As I continued to explore the island, I encountered more and more strange creatures, all affected by the [b]Serum[/b] – most of them hostile. But no matter what, I knew the [b]Growing Table[/b] was only a short-term solution. If I wanted more Serum, I had to get ready to fight for it.[/i]

notes.title: I have found something more sinister than I could ever imagine
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40377373/1e42352c12beefd17e248fc374649ad4815eb3f7.png[/img]

[i]As I wandered through the lush forest in search of resources, something caught my eye in the distance. A [b]dilapidated building[/b] with broken windows and an overgrown exterior stood out among the trees. Again, my curiosity got the best of me, and I decided to investigate.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40377373/590ecb4963d613c22b2c1883fab9fe7565e474d9.png[/img]

When I approached the building, a sense of unease washed over me. The front door was open, and I cautiously pushed it, stepping inside. The air was musty, and the only light came from the sun peeking through the cracks in the walls.

After my eyes adjusted to the darkness, I began to make out strange equipment scattered throughout the rooms. Tables with straps and restraints, jars filled with [b]unidentifiable liquids[/b], and medical tools that sent shivers down my spine. It was then that I noticed the paperwork tossed across the floor, with words like [b]"mutation"[/b], [b]"subject"[/b], and [b]“serum”[/b] scribbled across them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40377373/aca93da85f2d4578f92aa01735f6dd201411bd75.png[/img]

My heart raced as I realized the implications of what I had stumbled upon. This was a facility where [b]human tests[/b] were conducted. What horrors had occurred within these walls? Who were the subjects, and most importantly, was I one of them?[/i]

notes.title: The fauna of this island keeps surprising me
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40377373/08395c065e4d1ad14e85655264d91bcfd3399425.png[/img]

[i]From the first day, I found myself trapped in this strange place, I noticed that some plants carry the valuable Serum that helps me to stay alive. They are not the most sustainable source of this substance, but they provide just enough to get me through the day. 

What I discovered during my most recent expedition to the yet-undiscovered parts of the island shook me to the core. I came across a rather sizeable [b]tubular plant[/b] that seemed very… alive. I didn’t want to risk advancing towards it and kept observing from a distance.

After a short while, a family of [b]Rotten Rabbits[/b] approached the plant as if they wanted to try if it was edible. As soon as they got close enough, the plant exploded, launching its Serum-infused spores into the air. The rabbits fell almost immediately, but I was unsure if they were dead or incapacitated.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40377373/bda77b844cc61f630a3b219edc95280b1d9f8f2e.png[/img]

I could swear that with each minute, I spotted more and more of these plants as if they were reproducing rapidly. The truth was they were camouflaged well with the forest undergrowth, so I had to be extra careful with each subsequent step. 

I decided not to go any further and returned to my shelter. I need to make a plan on how to proceed. I must find a way around the plants if the spores are deadly. And even if they are not, they still might accelerate the mutation or, best case scenario, grant me a new ability. So many unknowns, yet I’m in no hurry to find out.

One thing that really makes me lose sleep is these plants must have grown from other seeds or spores, which means there is potentially a [b]much larger plant[/b] somewhere out there. I just hope I won’t cross paths with it.[/i]

notes.title: The story behind our name
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40377373/b67bcde2f6218e4ce2d1a171aef1f85ff0d19905.png[/img]

The Game Island team consists of passionate game designers, but above all – gamers. We want to create unforgettable games with original stories and freedom for the players in how they approach each task. [b]Serum[/b] is our first project and we’re happy to say that the development is progressing as planned, and there’s a lot we want to disclose in the near future.

[i]Part of the Game Island team:[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40377373/1d2e249d6c62d834a2591cf85f41e4532098bd34.png[/img]

Like with most studios out there, there’s a reason behind our name. And it’s actually quite simple. We’re called [b]Game Island[/b] because our studio is literally located on an island. Wyspa Słodowa (Słodowa Island) is a small island on the Odra river in Wrocław. Our office is located close to the river bank with a great view of Wroclaw.

You might think that a team located in a modern office would know little about survival, but we do have our daily struggles, like; being the first to arrive in the very limited parking lot, navigating the one-way narrow roads leading to the island, getting distracted by the surrounding nature or refilling the coffee machine.

All jokes aside, we love our office and we love making games. We know that by the time [b]Serum[/b] is finished, players will get to enjoy an immersive survival title that will keep them on the edge of their seats. Can’t wait to share more details.

[i]Fun fact about Wyspa Słodowa: it’s the only place in the centre of Wrocław where alcohol consumption is allowed in public.[/i]

[i]Just when I thought I had seen everything this strange land throws at me, I encountered another peculiar creature. For the sake of this journal, I will call it a Toxic Maggot since it shows some insect-like features. It resembles a mix of a tick and a crab when you look long enough.

These toxic insects have a nasty habit of biting and running away. I need to be very careful not to get overwhelmed by them since the bites are toxic and painful. They seem to like damp and dark places and primarily inhabit the underground part of these lands. They are, however, often spotted feasting on the carcass of dead animals.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40377373/584ae8fa91cb025ee07b565486cbf47b6e49fda0.png[/img]

Toxic Maggots are easy to kill – all you need is a sharp object and good timing. An element of surprise will indeed work to your benefit. Once I’ve disposed of the Maggots, I’ve found a good use for their dead bodies as they seem to attract larger predators.[/i]

notes.title: Serum Bestiary – Rotten Rabbits
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40377373/81a55a13c3aff3b5060466e7f4ef8c48b0d29b3a.png[/img]

[i]One of the first things I saw after waking up was the little hut house deep in the woods. At first, I couldn’t believe my own eyes, but inside the shed, I found a very useful crafting recipe for a serum that included Rotten Rabbit ears.

The lush woods surrounding the hut were a good place to start my hunt. With only the spear at my disposal, it was not an easy task as the Rotten Rabbits are very fast creatures. It took some patience and practice to get my first kill. Luckily, the Rabbits did not fight back – I can’t begin to imagine the consequences of a Rotten Rabbit bite, but I bet it would hurt like hell.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40377373/f0ef145e675a244ecbd82d48cc3c8f3d9703bcac.png[/img]

The recipe was very helpful for start, but the number of toxins in rabbit ears was very low, and that means I would need to start hunting for something bigger soon. However, I had the feeling that other animals roaming these lands would put up much greater of a fight. For now, these will have to do. Maybe I should think of some traps, to increase my chances of gathering more Rotten Rabbit ears? If only I could find a helpful recipe to craft some.[/i]

notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40377373/f835f360177aba2d3b275487bb2b49c5a5bbca41.png[/img]

[i]Setting up the trap was not an easy task. The rusty jaws had to be opened up until they were blocked entirely, and it had to be done with some serious power. I don't even want to mention that if you fail to open up the trap properly, you could lose a few fingers or the entire hand. It took me a while, but I finally managed to master this task in a matter of a few seconds. Now that the trap was set, it was time to place the stinky bait in the middle of it. I didn't know if I had enough. It was the first time that I tried to catch a Mist Wolf, and I was terrified and excited at the same time.

The place must have been right since I've seen the eyes of the animal here before. There looked like two torches flaming with green fire. It is a sight that I will remember to the end of my days, even if I tried my best to forget it. I wasn't about to stick around to wait for the Hound to arrive. No way in hell. Anyway, my Serum level was getting low, and I had to go back to my shelter for another shot.

A few minutes later, I heard a loud animal noise coming from where I had left the trap. Right away, I knew that this could be it. The Serum shot had to wait.

notes.title: Nature always finds a way
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40377373/70a6e7c83ae01ddc52a776ab38d9b4a144a67d74.png[/img]


[i]Darwin accumulated evidence showing that evolution on Earth had occurred and that living beings have changed drastically throughout history. He was right, and the place I’m in now is the best example of it. You would think that a highly toxic, poisonous substance like Serum could destroy everything it comes with contact with, but you would be wrong. 

I am not sure how long the plants and animals I found here have been exposed to the substance, but it was enough to alternate them in many different ways. The physical mutations are very apparent, and at first, I found them repulsive, but now since I’ve examined them closer, I think they’re unique and beautiful in their way. They have adapted to withstand the power of the chemical and use it to their advantage and produce it for their own needs. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40377373/43a8071b95d63619aaee6f7ffa5197190194c715.png[/img]


Unfortunately, Serum also alternates the minds of thinking creatures, making them a lot more aggressive and unpredictable in their behavior. The animals here are dangerous. They seem to have lost their sense of security, and most of them are never afraid to attack, even beings that are much larger and more dangerous than them. It feels like everything here is my enemy. 

I feel the changes Serum does to my body and my mind. Am I adapting to it? Is it helping me and making me stronger? Or am I just losing my mind? [/i]

notes.title: Something out there
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40377373/8c6b55cdd03604e614e78bc2abcd8418ec6b1a80.gif[/img]

[i]The day started well. It was sunny outside, and my pain was almost gone. For the first time in here, I felt like I was in control. I had my supplies, around ten traps set up outside the shelter if some uninvited guest wanted to visit me, and enough Serum to survive for a while. Plus, there were still two fume toad corpses hanging upside-down in the corner of the shed, ready for extraction. 

It was time for me to look for answers, to find the way out from this god-forsaken place. I went back to the spot I found the other day. There was still an entire wing of the building that I didn’t search. I went in through the big hole in the door that looked like a cannonball just went through it. It was pretty dark inside, but I could see that someone or something had trashed this place entirely. Floors were covered with broken equipment, cables were hanging from the ceiling, and radioactive warnings were posted all over the walls. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40377373/9e0418b73395e954fe96706b438502fcb39b1f2b.png[/img]

I gathered some stuff I thought I could use for my crafting table. I also found a journal that I couldn’t wait to read. When I was going back to the safe zone, It was already getting dark. I wasn’t far away from my shelter when I heard a high-pitched sound. I’ve heard it before. It was the last sound a fume toad makes before it dies. Another trap did its job, I thought to myself and went to examine it. 

I was surprised to see that my trap was untouched, but I saw something that scared the living thing out of me right next to it. An animal was feasting on a fume toad, a big one, looking like a mutated wolf, ripping the frog apart with its teeth. I froze in place, my hand tightly gripped on the wooden spear. The wolf looked up from above its prey, and our eyes met. 

Right then, I knew only one of us would make it home tonight. [/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40377373/1aa83cbd9c08b455e1c3eb3617089368fa14bf9f.png[/img]

[i]I placed my first trap on the west side of the lake, where croaking was always the laudest. I had to do it on a hot day so that the fume toads would be hiding from the burning sun. I carefully opened it up, and I’ve placed it down between two large bushes. Then I took out bait. It was a mix of leave and herbs that I know the animals were feeding on. I folded it into a ball and placed it gently in the center of the trap. My design wasn’t perfect, but it had to get the job done. I went back to the safe house full of hope. 

[b]I need my serum now, even more than before.[/b] [/i]

notes.title: Survivor's Diary #2 - Safe Zone
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40377373/06f35e609990a723bc87e377dac4b378191dbc84.png[/img]

[i]I don’t know if I was still being chased or not, but I kept on running through the dark forest. I remember being so tired that I couldn’t think about anything else but lay down and sleep right where I was, but my survival instinct told me that doing this would be certain death. Then I saw a shed. At first, I thought it was an illusion created by my confused mind, but I realized it was there. The small wooden house looked like it could fall apart any minute. I kicked the door open and went inside. I made sure I was alone, and right at that moment, I collapsed on the floor. 

I must have slept for a long time, and when I opened my eyes, it took me a while to process what I saw. Someone has covered the walls with snippets of paper that had all kinds of information on them. There were animal descriptions, maps of terrain, and even strange flower drawings that I have never seen before. All kinds of stuff cluttered the shed, and the most prominent object inside was a table with some sort of chemical equipment laid out on it. I also found some kind of animal trap, a broken spear with blood on it.

There was also a journal. I picked it up and started reading it right away. With every page, I felt more and more terrified. [/i]

notes.title: Flora #1 - Floral Fern
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40377373/2c0851b9f3a400f2c3a077a77df5c11e21be4ac2.png[/img]

[i]Finding out that plants can contain serum was a real surprise for me. It was even before I started setting up traps in the forest, that I was hunting Fume Toads with a spear. That day I couldn’t get close to one, no matter what. Attacking them when they were in a group was basically a suicide since I already felt very weak and in immediate need of an injection. 

I had to do it in a more sneaky way. I submerged in the stinky, shallow water of wetlands, and only with the top of my head sticking out, I waited. It must have been hours before I realized that my hunt was not going to be successful that day. When I decided to go back to my shelter, it was already pitch black. 

After a long wandering in the dark, I tripped over a tree root, fell forward right on my face, and passed out. I have no idea how long I was lying there, but when I opened my eyes, it was already getting light. Then I felt that horrible smell, that I’ve later learned to love.

Green leaves, strangely beautiful blue flowers, and a stench that couldn’t be confused with anything else - a large Floral Fern, the source of life, was right in front of me. [/i]

notes.title: Bestiary #1 - Fume Toad
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40377373/cb18e9fd561fb59cc83e18eb02417f28bc5021e3.png[/img]

[i]The first time I’ve heard that distinct croak, I was walking through the wetlands searching for some mechanical parts. I didn’t expect anything unusual, but I could smell something disturbing in the air. 

And then I saw it. Right away, I could tell that it wasn’t a regular frog. It was the size of a dog, with crazy eyes, sharp-looking teeth, and strange mushrooms covering its skin. The mushrooms were fuming with green vapor that seemed to be the source of that horrible, toxic smell.  

Then I heard another croak. And another right behind me. I dropped everything I’ve gathered and started running. That sound has been haunting me almost every night since...[/i]

notes.title: Survivor's Diary #1 - Crafting Table
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40377373/39ff68a8ac498ee964d9f53457bbe150950d6a64.png[/img]

[b]Day 1[/b]
I came across an abandoned building, I think it used to be a laboratory, about four miles to the north from here. I found an old table there in an and dragged it all the way back. I was lucky not to be seen with this big thing. It needs some fixing but it’s going to be perfect for the job. The time is running out, I need to hurry.

[b]Day 2[/b]
I went back to that building again and spent a few hours there searching for the stuff I needed for the distillation process. This time I wasn’t alone in that place and I almost fainted when I heard someone or something approaching. I didn’t make contact though, I guess I was lucky again.

[b]Day 3[/b]
The table is fixed. It’s stable and I have almost everything I need to finish the process, but I’m starting to feel sick. The pain that comes to me once in a few minutes is so bad I can’t even breathe. It wakes me up at night. Sometimes I can’t stop myself from screaming.

[b]Day 4[/b]
I was working all night. The pain is getting stronger and the attacks are coming more often. My body doesn’t even accept water anymore and I’m starting to hallucinate. I don’t know if I can survive it much longer. 

[b]Day 5 [/b]
It’s ready. The crafting table is done and I cried after I finished it. It can save me. It must. I’m too close. I can’t die. Not yet. There is just one last thing left to do. I need to find a donor.

notes.title: The Poison That Keeps You Alive
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40377373/79b94441bebfc7208416cf383abc31035c2668df.gif[/img]

[i]The morning was strangely quiet, although not everyone was lucky enough to enjoy it. The first rays of the sun shining through the forest revealed a figure sitting under a tree. It seemed like a tired man was resting there after a hard day’s work, but there was something off about him. He wasn’t moving at all. The skin on his bones was rotten, burned in a strange way, and in places seemed almost non-existent. Judging by his facial expression, one can think that before he died, he must have witnessed something horrible or experienced enormous pain. It could also be both of these things at once…[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40377373/f726b5d5ded1020feb62c20a35f8ff9dccf2619b.png[/img]

I approached him carefully, my head spinning around, eyes looking for any signs of a trap. My heart was pounding so hard, I could barely breathe.
 
“[b]It must be here somewhere. He must have it. Just a little. There’s no more time.[/b]”

notes.content:

This is when we took off with our project, Serum. From the very beginning, we were wondering how our main character should apply healing Serum. Should it be just by regular injection like in any other game or should we think about something “more”. 

That’s when we’ve developed the whole concept of the mysterious world, alien technology and the whole enigma around the serum.

notes.title: Serum - Trailer
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40377373/5144945cd373cb412fe39baaac8adae32247de5a.png[/img]

After you woke up, the first thing you’ve noticed was the mysterious plug with a timer on your arm. 
You realise quickly that to survive you will have to find the healing Serum. 

In our game, you’re intoxicated with a deadly virus that is slowly killing your body. The only way to survive is by applying a special serum that will extend your life by only a couple of hours.
You don’t know who and why but you know one thing. Life is in your hands now and your only choice is to race against the time.
Do you have what it takes to reveal the secrets of the mysterious Serum? Find out the truth about its creators and purpose!
